html:
The Tepehua are an Indigenous people of the Huasteca and the Sierra Norte where Hidalgo, Veracruz and Puebla meet in eastern Mexico. Their language is related to Totonac.

In 1492 their area lay between the Totonac, the Huastec and the Otomí, and much of it paid tribute to the Aztec Triple Alliance. They farm maize and coffee in the hills and are known for ritual paper cut figures and healing ceremonies. Only a few thousand people still speak Tepehua.
